cards.back: To look closely at something and notice things about it.
cards.say: observe. To look closely at something and notice things about it.

cards.back: To put things into groups.
cards.say: sort. To put things into groups.

cards.back: Things that are the same in some way.
cards.say: group. Things that are the same in some way.

cards.back: To say how many there are.
cards.say: count. To say how many there are.

cards.back: Looking alike in some way.
cards.say: same. Looking alike in some way.

cards.back: Not the same.
cards.say: different. Not the same.

cards.back: To look at two things and say how they are the same or different.
cards.say: compare. To look at two things and say how they are the same or different.

cards.back: A tool that makes small things look bigger.
cards.say: magnifying glass. A tool that makes small things look bigger.

cards.back: A mark you draw to count things. We make four marks, then a line across for five.
cards.say: tally. A mark you draw to count things. We make four marks, then a line across for five.

cards.front: Which tool helps you see a tiny ant better?
cards.back: A magnifying glass.
cards.say: Which tool helps you see a tiny ant better? A magnifying glass.

cards.front: Which sense do you use to observe colour?
cards.back: Sight.
cards.say: Which sense do you use to observe colour? Sight.

cards.back: By colour, by size or by how many holes.
cards.say: How can you sort buttons? By colour, by size or by how many holes.

cards.front: Sort these: dog, cat, rose. Which is a plant?
cards.back: The rose. A dog and a cat are animals.
cards.say: Sort these: dog, cat, rose. Which is a plant? The rose. A dog and a cat are animals.

cards.front: Sort these: spoon, fork, pillow. Which is soft?
cards.back: The pillow.
cards.say: Sort these: spoon, fork, pillow. Which is soft? The pillow.

cards.front: How many fingers are on two hands?
cards.back: Ten.
cards.say: How many fingers are on two hands? Ten.

cards.front: How many legs do two dogs have?
cards.back: Eight.
cards.say: How many legs do two dogs have? Eight.

cards.front: How are a cat and a dog the same?
cards.back: Both are animals with fur and four legs.
cards.say: How are a cat and a dog the same? Both are animals with fur and four legs.

cards.front: How are a bird and a fish different?
cards.back: A bird has wings and feathers. A fish has fins and scales.
cards.say: How are a bird and a fish different? A bird has wings and feathers. A fish has fins and scales.

cards.back: So we know how many there are.
cards.say: Why do we count things? So we know how many there are.

cards.back: It helps us find things and see what is the same.
cards.say: Why do we sort things? It helps us find things and see what is the same.

cards.front: What do we do first when we observe?
cards.back: We look carefully and notice things.
cards.say: What do we do first when we observe? We look carefully and notice things.

cards.front: What can you use to count with marks?
cards.back: A tally chart.
cards.say: What can you use to count with marks? A tally chart.
